claim: UNICEF/UNESCO/Save the Children reported on 19 March 2021 that security forces had reportedly occupied more than 60 schools and university campuses in 13 states and regions, worsening an education crisis already stressed by COVID-19 closures.
limitations: Reported facility occupation does not measure nationwide student participation or learning loss directly.

claim: UNICEF documented in September 2020 that Myanmar had developed digital curriculum support, teacher training and COVID-safe school-reopening guidance, including distribution to monastic, ethnic, migrant and displacement-related learning settings.
limitations: Shows pre-coup adaptive capacity and inclusion efforts; does not prove equal access or later continuity after the coup.

claim: OHCHR reported in 2021 that civil servants, students, political activists and defectors from police and military who opposed the coup had fled Myanmar, indicating cross-group displacement linked to political repression.
limitations: Qualitative report without a population denominator; cannot infer prevalence across all members of the named groups.

claim: ACLED methodology records the emergence after the coup of multiple anti-coup resistance actors, including NUG-aligned PDFs and other local defense groups that were not necessarily under NUG command.
limitations: Useful for actor differentiation; publication timing and historical dataset-version availability must be verified before early-cutoff use.

claim: ACLED describes some resistance groups forming alliances or cooperating with ethnic armed organizations while others remained outside NUG structures, supporting a model in which coalescence and fragmentation coexist.
limitations: Later methodology summarizes actor relations; contemporaneous evidence is required for each early snapshot and no alliance should be generalized to all groups.

claim: The school-occupation evidence is eventful and highly reportable, while ordinary functioning schools and routine teacher-student interactions are less newsworthy. The pilot therefore must not equate incident-report frequency with the national prevalence of educational disruption.
limitations: Methodological control only; contributes no historical pressure score.
